messages:
alex_customer: Hey team — customer running streaming completions via EventSource on Safari (macOS + iOS) is seeing repeated disconnects and a lot of partial outputs. They also reported a big spike in token charges due to reconnect loops. Repro steps below.

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you drop minimal repro + browser console logs? Is this Safari-only?

alex_customer: Safari only so far. Chrome/FF fine. Repro: page opens EventSource to /v1/streams?stream=true with Authorization via signed cookie. After a few seconds we sometimes get a 304 from the CDN mid-stream and the EventSource closes and reconnects repeatedly. Example curl I run: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?stream=true"
```
Response sequence shows initial 200 then later 304 and the connection effectively stops streaming. Client reconnects and gets another partial payload — billing increases.

eli_runtime: I’m looping in eng-runtime. A 304 mid-stream is suspicious — implies CDN cache behavior or cache-key mismatch. Do you have the raw response headers (x-edge-status, cf-cache-status, x-rw-request-id)? Also does the request hit an OPTIONS preflight that might alter forwarding rules?

jun_sre: Also check server headers: Cache-Control, Vary, Transfer-Encoding. If Vary omits Authorization, CDN might serve cached 304. Safari’s EventSource + prefetch behavior can be sensitive to missing keepalive/newline boundaries.

alex_customer: Pasting headers we captured: x-edge-status: 304, cf-cache-status: HIT, x-rw-request-id: rw_abc123. Response headers show: Vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin. No Vary: Authorization. Also noticed Content-Length absent on the mid-chunk response. Console shows repeated: "EventSource failed to connect" then open/close cycles.

sarah_edge: From the edge side: our CDN partner by default strips Authorization from cache key unless explicitly forwarded. We have a rule to forward Authorization for SSE routes but it looks like it was skipped because the request path matched a prefetch or OPTIONS rule. That could explain the 304. Also saw keep-alive semantics in the origin that might confuse intermediate caches.

maria_support: For an immediate workaround: 1) add a cache-busting query param to SSE URL (e.g., ?t=timestamp) or 2) ensure origin sends Cache-Control: no-store/no-cache for /v1/streams and add Vary: Authorization. Also ensure each SSE event ends with a full "\n\n" (Safari buffers otherwise).

eli_runtime: We’ll push a canary edge rule to pin SSE endpoints as origin-only (no cache) and explicitly include Authorization in cache key for those paths. Also adding a regression test to simulate 304 mid-stream should not close the client. Need edge logs and the request id (rw_abc123) — thanks for that.

jun_sre: Filed INC-2026-114 for tracking. @maria_support can you ask the customer to re-run with ?rw-client-debug=1 and upload logs? Also capturing proxy->origin timeouts and any 100-continue behavior helps.

alex_customer: Debug flag enabled, re-ran and uploaded logs here: https://files.redwood.example/attach/abc.log. Attached console screenshots too. We also noticed token billing jumped ~3x this morning during the reconnect bursts.

maria_support: Got the logs. We can see multiple short-lived reconnects with 304s from the edge in the middle of a stream. Immediate mitigation: we will apply an edge config to mark /v1/streams as uncacheable (canary in 30m). ETA to customer update: ~1 hour. Apologies for the impact :rotating_light:.

deploy-bot: deploy started — edge-rule/sse-no-cache (canary 10% → prod).

eli_runtime: After the canary I'll monitor token-billing metrics. If reconnects still cause duplicate billing, we’ll add a safety in the billing pipeline to dedupe repeated partial-stream token charges within a short window and discuss credits with finance. Also implementing LB-side reconnect-rate limiting with a Retry-After header to reduce storming.

alex_customer: Appreciate it. Please consider a billing credit — we saw a clear spike tied to this issue.

maria_support: We’ll loop in finance and issue a provisional credit while we investigate. For now please avoid manually refreshing the page during the canary.

jun_sre: Follow-ups for eng teams: add unit test that simulates 304 mid-stream and asserts stream remains open; ensure origin sends Transfer-Encoding: chunked + explicit keepalive comments, set Vary: Authorization for SSE endpoints. Filing PRs.

sarah_edge: Canary patch rolled to 10% and metrics look good so far — connection stability up, 304s dropped. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Closing the support loop in 24h unless you see any further disconnects. Thanks everyone for the quick response — will update on billing once finance replies.
